intent: Navigate from inside a sentence or a short line without changing the line it sits in.
typical_uses: A router link of the application, through `render`
A link to another site, with `external`

dont_use_when.situation: An action that does something rather than go somewhere
A whole row of a list that navigates
A trail of pages above a title

invariants.text: The anchor inherits font size, line height and weight and adds no height or padding, so a link inside a 14/20 line leaves the line box at 20.
Keyboard focus draws an outline on `--ring` at `--border-width-focus`; forced colours use Highlight.
`external` sets `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` unless the caller passes either, and appends an arrow icon with `aria-hidden`; the accessible wording stays with the caller.
Every variant draws the underline at rest; the inherit variant keeps the text's colour, so the underline is then the only thing that marks it as a link.

An svg placed directly in the link, the external arrow or the caller's own, is a 1em square on the text's baseline with a 0.25em gap on the text side, so it scales with the line. The rules carry no specificity, so a caller that sizes or spaces its icon keeps its own values.

anti_patterns.dont: Use `buttonVariants({ variant: 'link' })` for a link inside text
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use Link; the button variant carries a control's height and padding into the line

anti_patterns.dont: Import the router into the kit to navigate
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass the application's router link through `render`

render.states: render replaces the anchor with one the caller supplies
render.because: useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (Link passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is how the application's router link takes the link's class and props.

bad.title: A link that performs an action
bad.why: An anchor without a destination is not a link; use Button.

companions.typed_by: cva(...), returns (props: VariantProps<typeof linkVariants> & { className?: string }) => string
companions.description: The variant class-name builder Link itself uses, for a router component that cannot take `render`.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}> | undefined.
